name: Summary Judgment Plan
description: Store imported Covidence human screening decisions once per article and compare them against derived AI summary answers while preserving granular AI prompt-level review detail.

userStories.title: Add summary-mode schema and storage tables
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want an explicit project judgment mode and a dedicated human summary table so future Covidence imports can store one human screening decision per article without overloading prompt-level tables.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `app.project.human_judgment_mode` with default `prompt` and a check restricting values to `prompt` or `summary`.
Add `criteria_disposition`, `criteria_section_key`, and `criteria_section_label` to `app.project_prompt`, with a check that limits `criteria_disposition` to `include`, `exclude`, or `NULL`.

Create `app.judgment_human_summary` with `UNIQUE(project_id, article_id)`, project/article lookup indexes, and checks that restrict `answer` to `yes`, `no`, `maybe`, or `NULL` and `origin` to `covidence_import` or `manual_override`.
The new summary table supports a later manual override path via `origin = 'manual_override'` even though no override UI ships in this first pass.
The migration is future-imports-only and does not backfill or auto-upgrade existing projects.

userStories.title: Add the strict summary derivation helper
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want one shared summary-answer helper so AI and human summary views use the same deterministic inclusion and exclusion rule everywhere.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a shared helper that accepts enabled prompt criteria metadata plus normalized answers and returns `yes`, `no`, `maybe`, or `null`.
The helper returns `no` when any exclusion answer is `yes` or any inclusion answer is `no`.
The helper returns `maybe` when no hard-`no` applies and any answer is `maybe`, and returns `yes` only when all inclusions are `yes` and all exclusions are `no`.
Missing answers return `null`, and zero-inclusion or zero-exclusion projects resolve cleanly without special-case UI logic.
If a summary-mode project has an enabled prompt without criteria metadata, the helper returns `null` and triggers a clear warning instead of guessing.

userStories.title: Import new Covidence projects in summary mode
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want new structured Covidence screening projects to seed one article-level human summary row so imported human decisions match how Covidence was actually reviewed.
acceptanceCriteria: The structured Covidence create and sync path sets `project.human_judgment_mode = 'summary'` for newly created screening projects.
Project prompt links persist `criteria_disposition`, `criteria_section_key`, and `criteria_section_label` in stable import order.
Summary-mode Covidence seeding writes one `app.judgment_human_summary` row per imported article with `origin = 'covidence_import'` and the existing stage-based answer.
Summary-mode Covidence import no longer seeds duplicated prompt rows into `app.judgment_human`.
Existing pre-change projects remain prompt mode because this first pass is future-imports-only.

userStories.title: Extend mart and OLAP with summary-mode answers
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want review-serving data to surface human and LLM summaries so list views can compare overall decisions without recomputing them client-side.
acceptanceCriteria: Summary-mode rollups read `app.judgment_human_summary` for human completeness while prompt-mode rollups keep using `app.judgment_human`.
Serving and OLAP paths expose `humanSummaryAnswer` and `llmSummaryAnswer` for summary-mode articles.
AI summary derivation uses only enabled summary-eligible prompts and the shared strict rule.
`has_all_human_answers` remains available but becomes mode-aware: summary-row presence in summary mode and prompt-count completeness in prompt mode.

userStories.title: Expose summary-mode review API contracts
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the review routes to return explicit summary-mode fields so the client never has to infer summary behavior from missing prompt-level data.
acceptanceCriteria: Article review detail returns `humanJudgmentMode`, `humanSummaryAnswer`, `llmSummaryAnswer`, and prompt criteria metadata for summary-mode projects.
`articlesreviewsboth` returns `humanJudgmentMode`, `humanSummaryAnswer`, and `llmSummaryAnswer` for summary-mode rows and omits prompt-derived `humanAnswersByPrompt`.
`articlesreviewshuman` and `articlesreviewshumanfilters` switch to an overall-summary contract in summary mode instead of prompt-by-prompt human judgment arrays and filters.
Client branching depends on the explicit mode field rather than nullable prompt-level fields.

userStories.title: Show summary-only comparison labels in review UI
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I want summary-mode review screens to compare the overall human and AI decisions while still letting me inspect the AI's per-criterion reasoning.
acceptanceCriteria: The review sidebar shows an overall decision card with human and AI summary answers for summary-mode projects.
In summary mode, the `reviews both` right-side comparison label uses only `llmSummaryAnswer` and `humanSummaryAnswer`.
The compact `Y`, `N`, `M` label style and existing green, yellow, and red agreement coloring are preserved for summary-vs-summary comparisons.
Prompt chips remain visible as AI detail only, and summary mode does not append per-prompt human comparison letters.
Summary-mode human review screens use overall-answer row labels and filters that match the new API contract.

userStories.title: Block prompt-based human assessment for summary mode
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want summary-mode projects to bypass prompt-based human assessment routes so the app cannot create misleading per-prompt pending rows for a summary-only workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: `HumanAssessmentRoutes` init returns a clear `409` or `400` for summary-mode projects before creating any pending `app.judgment_human` rows.
`HumanAssessmentRoutes` submit returns a clear `409` or `400` for summary-mode projects instead of validating prompt-level answers.
Prompt-mode projects keep their existing init and submit behavior.
The prompt-based human assessment UI flow is not exposed for summary-mode projects.

userStories.title: Lock summary-mode behavior with regression coverage
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want targeted regression coverage for summary-mode imports, serving, routes, and UI so future changes cannot reintroduce fake prompt-level human comparisons.
acceptanceCriteria: Add Covidence import coverage proving summary-mode projects seed `judgment_human_summary`, persist criteria metadata, and do not seed duplicated `judgment_human` rows.
Add mart and OLAP coverage proving summary-mode projects compute human completeness from the summary table and expose `humanSummaryAnswer` and `llmSummaryAnswer`.
Add route parity and review detail coverage proving summary-mode payloads return the explicit mode field and omit fake per-prompt human answer maps.
Add human-route and human-assessment-route coverage proving summary-mode human list and filter endpoints use overall answers and prompt-based human assessment is rejected cleanly.
Add review-table or component coverage proving the right-side comparison label uses summary-vs-summary `Y`, `N`, or `M` values while AI prompt detail still renders.
